question: Brihadiswara Temple which exhibits Dravidian temple architecture is located in __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thanjavur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Brihadeeswarar Temple (also called Rajarajeswaram or Peruvudaiyar Kovil) is located in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu. (बृहदीश्वर मंदिर — तंजावुर)

 

• It was built by the Chola king Raja Raja Chola I and completed around 1010 CE, dedicated to Lord Shiva.

 

• It is one of the largest South Indian temples and an outstanding example of Dravidian temple architecture, with a massive vimana (tower) about 66 metres tall.

 

• Along with the Brihadeeswarar temples at Gangaikonda Cholapuram and Airavatesvara at Darasuram, it forms part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Great Living Chola Temples".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The temple's vimana casts almost no shadow at noon, and the massive Nandi (bull) statue at its entrance is carved from a single stone.

 

NOTE

 

• Dharmapuri (Option 2): A district in Tamil Nadu, not associated with the Brihadeeswarar Temple.

 

• Madurai (Option 3): Known for the Meenakshi Amman Temple, not the Brihadeeswarar Temple.

 

• Thiruvanathapuram (Option 4): Capital of Kerala, known for the Padmanabhaswamy Temple, unrelated to this Chola temple.

question: In cricket, ________ is called by the umpire when the bowler doesn’t deliver the ball within reach of the batter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is wide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A wide is called by the umpire when the ball is bowled too far from the batter (out of normal reach) for the batter to be able to play a normal cricket shot. (वाइड बॉल — क्रिकेट का नियम)

 

• It results in one extra run being added to the batting team's total, and the delivery must be re-bowled as it does not count as one of the over's six legitimate balls.

 

• This is distinct from a no ball, which is called for other infringements such as overstepping the popping crease or bowling above waist height.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Laws of Cricket (Law 22) govern what constitutes a wide; umpires signal it by extending both arms horizontally.

 

NOTE

 

• Dead ball (Option 2): Called when play is temporarily suspended, e.g., when the ball comes to rest or is out of play.

 

• No ball (Option 3): Called for illegitimate deliveries such as overstepping the crease, not for a ball out of the batter's reach.

 

• Yorker (Option 4): A type of delivery that pitches near the batter's feet; it is a bowling technique, not an umpire's call.

question: Which of the following rocky planets is the fastest planet in our solar system – traveling through space at about 29 miles (47 kilometres) per second?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mercury.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and has the fastest orbital speed among the planets, moving at about 47 km/s (≈29 miles/second). (बुध ग्रह — सबसे तेज़ ग्रह)

 

• Because of the Sun's strong gravitational pull at its close distance (about 58 million km), Mercury completes one orbit of the Sun in just about 88 Earth days.

 

• Mercury is also the smallest planet in the solar system and has no natural satellite.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Orbital speed decreases with distance from the Sun; Neptune, the farthest planet, has the slowest orbital speed (about 5.4 km/s).

 

NOTE

 

• Earth (Option 1): Orbits the Sun at about 29.8 km/s, slower than Mercury.

 

• Venus (Option 2): Orbits at about 35 km/s, slower than Mercury.

 

• Mars (Option 3): Orbits at about 24 km/s, slower than Mercury.

question: Who among the following rulers was a part of the Tripartite Struggle for the possession of Kannauj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dharmapala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tripartite Struggle (8th–9th century CE) was a three-way contest for control of Kannauj, fought among the Pala, Pratihara, and Rashtrakuta dynasties. (त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष — कन्नौज)

 

• Dharmapala, the second and most powerful ruler of the Pala dynasty of Bengal, was one of the three principal contenders in this struggle, along with the Pratiharas and the Rashtrakutas.

 

• Dharmapala installed his protégé Chakrayudha on the throne of Kannauj for a time, before control eventually passed to the Rashtrakutas and Pratiharas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tripartite Struggle continued for nearly two centuries, and the Gurjara-Pratiharas eventually emerged dominant, holding Kannauj as their capital.

 

NOTE

 

• Yashovarman (Option 2): An earlier king of Kannauj (8th century) defeated by Lalitaditya of Kashmir; his reign predates the Tripartite Struggle proper.

 

• Mahendrapal (Option 3): A later Pratihara ruler (successor of Mihira Bhoja), not one of the three original contenders of the struggle.

 

• Prithvi Raj III (Option 4): A 12th-century Chahamana (Chauhan) ruler of Delhi and Ajmer, unrelated to the 8th–9th century Tripartite Struggle.

question: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote a novel Anand Math based on which of the following rebellions/revolts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanyasi Rebellion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's novel *Anandmath* (1882) is based on the Sannyasi (Fakir-Sannyasi) Rebellion of the late 18th century. (आनंदमठ — संन्यासी विद्रोह)

 

• The novel is set against the backdrop of armed sannyasis and fakirs in Bengal resisting Company rule and famine-era exploitation, and it introduced the song "Vande Mataram", later adopted as India's National Song.

 

• The Sannyasi Rebellion (c. 1770s–1800s) was one of the earliest armed uprisings against British East India Company rule in Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• "Vande Mataram" from Anandmath was adopted as the National Song of India by the Constituent Assembly in 1950.

 

NOTE

 

• Mappila Rebellion (Option 1): A series of uprisings by Mappila Muslims in Malabar, unrelated to Anandmath.

 

• Paika Rebellion (Option 2): An 1817 uprising by Paikas (traditional militia) of Odisha against the British, not the subject of Anandmath.

 

• Kuki Revolt (Option 4): An uprising (1917–19) by the Kuki people of Manipur/Northeast India, unrelated to the novel.

question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT vis-à-vis Fundamental Duties?

1) They are obligatory in nature

2) Fundamental Rights and Fundamental duties are complementary to each other.

3) The introduction of Article 51A created strong base for a concrete national character and strong harmony.

4) Eleventh fundamental duty was added by 78th constitutional amendment act.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 4.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 4 is factually incorrect: the eleventh Fundamental Duty — the duty of a parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child/ward between the ages of 6 and 14 years — was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, not the 78th. (मूल कर्तव्य — 86वां संविधान संशोधन)

 

• Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A) are civic obligations expected of every citizen, and they are considered complementary to Fundamental Rights.

 

• Article 51A was inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, to strengthen national character and social harmony.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Originally, ten Fundamental Duties were listed; the eleventh was added in 2002 by the 86th Amendment (the same amendment that made education a fundamental right under Article 21A).

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 (Option 1): Incorrectly flags statements 1 and 2 as wrong, though both are accurate statements about Fundamental Duties.

 

• 2 and 3 (Option 2): Incorrectly flags statements 2 and 3 as wrong, though both are accurate.

 

• Only 3 (Option 3): Incorrectly flags statement 3 as wrong, though the 42nd Amendment did strengthen national character via Article 51A.

question: The phenomenon of the interaction between nonallelic genes at two or more loci resulting in one gene masking the phenotypic expression of another gene, is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is epistasis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Epistasis is the phenomenon where a gene at one locus (the epistatic gene) masks or suppresses the phenotypic expression of a gene at another, non-allelic locus (the hypostatic gene). (एपिस्टासिस — जीन अंतःक्रिया)

 

• It is a form of gene interaction between non-allelic genes and can alter classical Mendelian dihybrid ratios (e.g., 9:3:3:1 can become ratios like 9:3:4, 12:3:1, or 9:7).

 

• A classic example is coat colour in Labrador retrievers, where one gene determines whether a second, separate colour gene is expressed at all.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Epistasis differs from simple dominance, which involves two alleles of the same gene (locus), not two different genes.

 

NOTE

 

• Linkage (Option 1): Refers to genes located close together on the same chromosome tending to be inherited together, not one gene masking another.

 

• Complete inheritance/dominance (Option 2): Refers to one allele of the same gene completely masking the other allele at that same locus.

 

• Incomplete inheritance (Option 4): Refers to a blended phenotype when neither allele of the same gene is fully dominant, unrelated to interaction between different genes.

question: Sanjukta Panigrahi a legendary dancer is associated with which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sanjukta Panigrahi (1944–1997) was a legendary exponent of Odissi classical dance from Odisha. (संजुक्ता पाणिग्रही — ओडिसी नृत्य)

 

• She trained under Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and was instrumental in reviving and popularising Odissi as a classical dance form on national and international stages.

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Shri (1975) and Padma Bhushan (1987) for her contribution to Indian classical dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known Odissi exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh, and Madhavi Mudgal.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihu (Option 1): A folk dance of Assam, unrelated to Sanjukta Panigrahi.

 

• Laho (Option 2): A folk dance of Meghalaya, unrelated to her.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 3): A classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, a different tradition from Odissi.

question: _____ was appointed British High Commissioner to India in April 2024.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lindy Cameron.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lindy Cameron was appointed as the British High Commissioner to India in April 2024, becoming the first woman to hold this post. (लिंडी कैमरन — ब्रिटिश उच्चायुक्त, भारत)

 

• Before this appointment, she served as CEO of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC).

 

• As High Commissioner, she is based at the British High Commission in New Delhi and oversees UK-India diplomatic, trade, and security relations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India and the UK maintain a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, established in 2021, covering trade, defence, health, education and technology cooperation.

 

NOTE

 

• Nicholas Fenn (Option 1): A former British High Commissioner to India, but not the officeholder appointed in April 2024.

 

• Philip Barton (Option 2): A former British High Commissioner to India, but not the officeholder appointed in April 2024.

 

• Dominic Asquith (Option 4): A former British High Commissioner to India, but not the officeholder appointed in April 2024.

question: Pinjore heritage festival is organised by the state of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pinjore Heritage Festival is organised by the state of Haryana at the historic Yadavindra Gardens (Pinjore Gardens) in Panchkula district. (पिंजौर विरासत महोत्सव — हरियाणा)

 

• The gardens were laid out in the Mughal garden style, associated with Fidai Khan (a foster-brother of Aurangzeb) and later renovated under the Patiala rulers.

 

• The festival showcases Haryana's folk culture, music, dance, crafts and cuisine, promoting heritage tourism in the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Haryana also hosts the Surajkund International Crafts Mela, another major heritage/cultural festival held annually at Surajkund, Faridabad.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand (Option 1): Not associated with the Pinjore Heritage Festival; known for festivals like Sarhul and Karma.

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 2): Not associated with this festival; known for festivals like the Kumbh Mela and Nanda Devi Raj Jat.

 

• Sikkim (Option 3): Not associated with this festival; known for festivals like Losar and Saga Dawa.

question: In Microsoft Word, which option allows you to exclude specific sections or types of text from the spelling and grammar check?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Exclusion Dictionary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft Word, the Exclusion Dictionary feature allows a user to exclude specific words, sections, or types of text from the spelling and grammar check. (एक्सक्लूज़न डिक्शनरी — वर्तनी जाँच)

 

• Words or text configured for exclusion are then flagged or skipped by the spelling and grammar checker, letting users customise which content is checked.

 

• This is distinct from the standard custom dictionary, which adds words so they are treated as correctly spelled; an exclusion dictionary instead works to exclude terms from being treated as such.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Word also allows marking selected text with "Do not check spelling or grammar" under language settings, another way to skip proofing for specific text.

 

NOTE

 

• Spell check (Option 1): The general feature that checks spelling errors across the document; it does not itself provide exclusion of sections.

 

• AutoCorrect (Option 2): Automatically corrects common typing errors as you type; it does not exclude text from spelling/grammar checks.

 

• Thesaurus (Option 4): Provides synonyms and antonyms for words; unrelated to spelling/grammar exclusion.

question: As per Census of India 2011, which of the following groups of states recorded the lowest literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar and Arunachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, Bihar recorded the lowest literacy rate among all states at about 61.8%, followed by Arunachal Pradesh at about 65.4%. (जनगणना 2011 — बिहार, सबसे कम साक्षरता)

 

• Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate (about 93.9%) among states.

 

• The national literacy rate as per Census 2011 was about 74.04% (male: 82.14%, female: 65.46%).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other relatively low-literacy states in 2011 included Rajasthan (~66.1%) and Jharkhand (~66.4%), close behind Bihar and Arunachal Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan and Assam (Option 1): Assam's 2011 literacy rate (~72.2%) was well above the lowest states, so this pairing is incorrect.

 

• Rajasthan and Jharkhand (Option 3): Both had somewhat higher literacy rates than Bihar and Arunachal Pradesh in 2011.

 

• Bihar and Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): Madhya Pradesh's literacy rate (~69.3%) was notably higher than Arunachal Pradesh's.

question: The Maritime Anti-Piracy Act, 2022, was enacted to give effect to which of the following?
option_1: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea relating to repression of piracy on high seas.
option_2: United Nations Convention on Oceans and Seas relating to repression of piracy on high seas.
option_3: United Nations Regional seas convention relating to repression of piracy on high seas.
option_4: United Nations Treaty on Oceans relating to repression of piracy on high seas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea relating to repression of piracy on high seas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Maritime Anti-Piracy Act, 2022 was enacted by India to give effect to the provisions of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), 1982, relating to the repression of piracy on the high seas. (समुद्री लूट रोधी अधिनियम 2022 — UNCLOS)

 

• The Act defines piracy, prescribes punishment (including life imprisonment or death in cases involving murder or attempted murder), and empowers Indian authorities to try and punish piracy committed on the high seas, even by foreign nationals.

 

• It strengthens India's ability to combat piracy, especially given incidents in areas such as the Gulf of Aden.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• UNCLOS, 1982, is often called the "Constitution for the Oceans" and governs maritime zones, navigation rights, and the use of the seas and their resources.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4: These refer to fictitious/non-existent instruments ("Convention on Oceans and Seas", "Regional Seas Convention", "Treaty on Oceans") — no such UN conventions on piracy exist; UNCLOS is the actual instrument the Act gives effect to.

question: With which of the following sports is Lovlina Borgohain associated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is boxing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lovlina Borgohain is an Indian boxer from Assam who won the bronze medal in the women's welterweight category at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics. (लवलीना बोरगोहेन — मुक्केबाज़ी)

 

• She also won a bronze medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics in the women's 75 kg category, becoming a two-time Olympic medallist.

 

• She has also won medals at the World Boxing Championships and Asian Games, and has been honoured with the Padma Shri.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other prominent Indian Olympic boxing medallists include Mary Kom and Vijender Singh.

 

NOTE

 

• Hockey (Option 1): Not Lovlina Borgohain's sport.

 

• Cricket (Option 2): Not her sport.

 

• Basketball (Option 3): Not her sport.

question: Which of the following states has mangrove forests?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Andhra Pradesh has significant mangrove forests, notably the Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary in the Godavari-Krishna delta, one of India's largest mangrove ecosystems after the Sundarbans. (कोरिंगा मैंग्रोव — आंध्र प्रदेश)

 

• Mangroves grow in coastal intertidal zones with brackish water; Andhra Pradesh's long coastline along the Bay of Bengal supports such ecosystems.

 

• Other Indian states/UTs with notable mangroves include West Bengal (Sundarbans), Gujarat, Maharashtra, Odisha (Bhitarkanika), and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's mangrove cover is assessed periodically in the India State of Forest Report; West Bengal has the largest mangrove cover in the country.

 

NOTE

 

• Telangana (Option 1): A landlocked state with no coastline, so it cannot have mangrove forests.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): A landlocked, largely arid state with no coastline or mangroves.

 

• Manipur (Option 4): A landlocked northeastern state with no coastline or mangroves.

question: Which state hosts the Nehru trophy boat race?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nehru Trophy Boat Race is held annually on the Punnamada Lake in Alappuzha (Alleppey), Kerala. (नेहरू ट्रॉफी वल्लमकली — केरल)

 

• It features traditional snake boats (chundan vallam) and is one of the most popular snake boat races (vallam kali) in Kerala, usually held on the second Saturday of August.

 

• The trophy was instituted after Jawaharlal Nehru rode in a snake boat during a visit to Alappuzha in 1952 and was so impressed that he donated a trophy for the winning boat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala's backwaters host several other boat races, such as the Champakulam Moolam Boat Race and the Aranmula Boat Race.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Not associated with the Nehru Trophy Boat Race.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): Not associated with this race.

 

• Goa (Option 4): Not associated with this race.

question: Which of the following devices is used to accelerate charged particles to high velocities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is cyclotron.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A cyclotron is a type of particle accelerator that uses a static magnetic field and an oscillating electric field to accelerate charged particles (such as protons) to high velocities, moving them along a spiral path. (साइक्लोट्रॉन — आवेशित कणों का त्वरक)

 

• It was invented by Ernest Lawrence in 1932, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1939.

 

• Cyclotrons are used in nuclear physics research and in producing radioisotopes for medical applications such as PET imaging.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre (VECC) is located in Kolkata.

 

NOTE

 

• Cryotron (Option 1): A switching device based on superconductivity, used in computing circuits, not a particle accelerator.

 

• Copatron (Option 2): Not a recognised particle-accelerating device; a distractor term.

 

• Cosmotron (Option 3): A specific large proton synchrotron built at Brookhaven National Laboratory in the 1950s; the generic device classically associated with accelerating charged particles is the cyclotron, which is the intended answer here.

question: Which of the following options is INCORRECT?
option_1: Distinguished economists from India and abroad were invited to advise on India’s economic development during the first five-year plan period.
option_2: India borrowed the idea of five-year plans from the former Soviet Union.
option_3: The Planning Commission of India was set up in 1950.
option_4: The chairmanship of the Planning Commission of India was given to the Prime Minister.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Distinguished economists from India and abroad were invited to advise on India’s economic development during the first five-year plan period.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This statement is incorrect: the invitation of internationally distinguished economists to advise on India's economic development is chiefly associated with the formulation of the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61), based on the Mahalanobis model, not the First Plan. (द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना — विदेशी अर्थशास्त्री)

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951–56), based largely on the Harrod-Domar model, focused on agriculture, irrigation and power, with comparatively limited direct foreign-economist consultation.

 

• Statements 2, 3 and 4 are factually correct: India's five-year plans were modelled on the Soviet Union's Gosplan; the Planning Commission was set up in 1950; and the Prime Minister has always been the ex-officio Chairman of the Planning Commission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in January 2015.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (borrowed idea from Soviet Union): This is a correct statement, so it is not the answer.

 

• Option 3 (Planning Commission set up in 1950): This is a correct statement, so it is not the answer.

 

• Option 4 (PM as Chairman): This is a correct statement, so it is not the answer.

question: In which of the following states are the Pai songs accompanied by the Saria dance sung during the rain festivals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Madhya Pradesh, Pai songs are traditionally sung accompanied by the Saria dance during the rain (monsoon) festivals among local/tribal communities of the state. (पाई गीत, सरिया नृत्य — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• Madhya Pradesh has a rich tradition of tribal and folk performing arts tied to the agricultural calendar, with songs and dances performed to celebrate the onset of the monsoon and the sowing season.

 

• Such performances reflect the close relationship between folk culture and agrarian life in the state's tribal belts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Madhya Pradesh include Karma, Saila, Matki, and Grida.

 

NOTE

 

• Sikkim (Option 1): Not associated with Pai songs/Saria dance; known for dances like Chu Faat and Singhi Chaam.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): Not associated with this tradition; known for dances like Raslila and Kajri songs.

 

• Tripura (Option 3): Not associated with this tradition; known for dances like Hojagiri and Garia.

question: The relationship between which of the following is correct?
option_1: NDP at market price = GDP at market price + depreciation
option_2: Domestic income = NDP at market price + net indirect taxes
option_3: GDP at market price = price + quantity of final goods and services
option_4: National income = NDP at factor cost + net factor income from abroad
solution_text:
The correct answer is National income = NDP at factor cost + net factor income from abroad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Income (NNP at factor cost) is correctly derived as: NNP at factor cost = NDP at factor cost + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). (राष्ट्रीय आय — शुद्ध विदेशी कारक आय)

 

• NFIA equals income earned by residents from abroad minus income earned by non-residents within the domestic territory.

 

• This identity correctly links the domestic measure of income (NDP at factor cost) to the national measure (National Income at factor cost) by adjusting for income flows across borders.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The correct relation involving depreciation is: NDP at market price = GDP at market price − Depreciation (subtraction, not addition).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrect because NDP at market price = GDP at market price − depreciation, not plus; depreciation is subtracted to move from a gross to a net measure.

 

• Option 2: Incorrect because Domestic income (NDP at factor cost) = NDP at market price − net indirect taxes, not plus.

 

• Option 3: Incorrect because GDP at market price is the sum of (price × quantity) of final goods and services, not price plus quantity.

question:
Match the states in column A to their ports in column B.

Column A (States): 1. Goa   2. West Bengal   3. Tamil Nadu   4. Gujarat

Column B (Ports): a. Mormugao Port   b. Kandla Port   c. Tuticorin Port   d. Haldia Port
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-a, 2-d, 3-c, 4-b.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Goa's major port is Mormugao Port (1-a); West Bengal's major port here is Haldia Port (2-d); Tamil Nadu's major port here is Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar) Port (3-c); and Gujarat's major port here is Kandla (Deendayal) Port (4-b). (प्रमुख बंदरगाह — राज्य मिलान)

 

• Mormugao Port in Goa is historically significant for iron ore exports and is one of India's major ports.

 

• Kandla Port (renamed Deendayal Port) in Gujarat is a key western-coast port handling bulk cargo.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has several major ports beyond those above, including Mumbai, Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva), Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Paradip, Cochin, New Mangalore, and Kolkata.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (1-a, 2-d, 3-b, 4-c): Incorrectly swaps the ports for Tamil Nadu and Gujarat.

 

• Option 3 (1-d, 2-a, 3-c, 4-b): Incorrectly swaps the ports for Goa and West Bengal.

 

• Option 4 (1-a, 2-c, 3-d, 4-b): Incorrectly swaps the ports for West Bengal and Tamil Nadu.

question: The 42nd amendment of the Indian Constitution added ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fundamental duties.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, added Part IVA (Article 51A) to the Constitution, laying down the Fundamental Duties of citizens. (42वां संविधान संशोधन — मूल कर्तव्य)

 

• This amendment, enacted during the Emergency (1975–77), is often called a "Mini-Constitution" because of the sweeping changes it made.

 

• It also added the words "Socialist", "Secular", and "Integrity" to the Preamble, among other changes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fundamental Duties were based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

NOTE

 

• Legislature (Option 1): Not something "added" by a specific amendment in this sense; legislatures are original constitutional bodies.

 

• Fundamental rights (Option 2): Fundamental Rights were part of the original Constitution (Part III, 1950), not added by the 42nd Amendment.

 

• National anthem (Option 4): The National Anthem was adopted by the Constituent Assembly in 1950, not added by the 42nd Amendment.

question: Who among the following is a singer of Hindustani classical music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shubha Mudgal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shubha Mudgal is a renowned Hindustani classical vocalist, trained in the Gwalior, Jaipur-Atrauli and Kirana gharana traditions. (शुभा मुद्गल — हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत)

 

• She has received the Padma Shri for her contribution to Hindustani classical and semi-classical (thumri, dadra) music.

 

• The other three named artistes — Aruna Sairam, Sudha Ragunathan, and S. Sowmya — are all noted exponents of Carnatic classical music, the classical tradition of South India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hindustani classical music (North Indian tradition) and Carnatic classical music (South Indian tradition) are the two major classical music systems of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Aruna Sairam (Option 1): A celebrated Carnatic vocalist, not Hindustani.

 

• Sudha Ragunathan (Option 2): A celebrated Carnatic vocalist, not Hindustani.

 

• S Sowmya (Option 3): A celebrated Carnatic vocalist and veena player, not Hindustani.

question: Which organisation, in collaboration with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), and the Ministry of Education, announced the launch of the ‘AI For All’ initiative with the purpose of creating a basic understanding of artificial intelligence for everyone in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Intel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Intel, in collaboration with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) and the Ministry of Education, launched the "AI For All" initiative to create basic awareness and understanding of artificial intelligence among the general public in India. (एआई फॉर ऑल — इंटेल और सीबीएसई)

 

• The initiative was launched as a free online course aimed at students, teachers, and citizens with no prior technical background, to build foundational AI literacy.

 

• It builds on Intel and CBSE's earlier collaboration on the "AI For Youth" curriculum introduced in schools.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• CBSE has also partnered with other technology companies on skill-development initiatives, including coding and AI curricula for school students.

 

NOTE

 

• Infosys (Option 2): An Indian IT company known for its own skilling initiatives (e.g., Infosys Springboard), but not the partner behind "AI For All" with CBSE.

 

• TCS (Option 3): A major Indian IT company with its own CSR/education programmes, but not the partner behind "AI For All".

 

• IBM (Option 4): A global tech company with AI initiatives of its own, but not the partner behind the CBSE "AI For All" programme.

question: Rows in MS-Excel are identified by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is numbers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft Excel, rows are identified by numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), while columns are identified by letters (A, B, C, ...). (एक्सेल में पंक्तियाँ — संख्याओं द्वारा पहचान)

 

• Each cell in a worksheet is referenced by combining its column letter and row number, e.g., cell A1 refers to the intersection of column A and row 1.

 

• In modern versions of Excel (2007 onward), a worksheet has 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The last column in a modern Excel worksheet is labelled XFD (the 16,384th column).

 

NOTE

 

• Letters (Option 1): This describes how columns, not rows, are identified.

 

• Numbers with letters (Option 2): This describes a cell reference (e.g., A1), not how rows alone are identified.

 

• Timings (Option 4): Not related to how rows are identified in Excel.
